Verification 1.1 already establishes x2=0 and reduced cost -1, and 2.1 gives d=-1, r=(1,1), Ar=0 and c^Tr=-1. Hence x(B)+t r is feasible for all t>=0 and its cost tends to minus infinity. Wrote the full vector (1,0,1,0,2,0,0), which satisfies all three equations and has cost -1. Restored the feasible-pivot hypotheses, leaving tie rule and final optimality clause in F1/F2; the numerical proof was already sound, so this is nonfatal.

The rejection correctly distinguishes an arbitrary optimal basic point from a dual-feasible basis, but this proof uses the specific Phase I driver in F1: alg-revised-simplex-phase-one calls Bland, whose instruction 1 returns optimal only after every nonbasic reduced cost is nonnegative. Thus step 1.2 has that stopping-test premise from F1, not merely optimality from F2; basic reduced costs are zero by the dictionary. For costs (0,1), this gives (DA)^Ty<=0 and (Db)^Ty=w*>0, hence q=-D^Ty has the claimed signs. The identity-augmented system is full row rank and its objective is bounded below. Zero optimum forces every artificial value zero; a nonzero extraction pivot preserves that feasible point, while a deleted transformed original equation is exactly 0=0. Each removal reduces the artificial-basic count, including empty/rank-deficient cases. No repair is needed.
